plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 4: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
plan.contextChunk: This figure presents a single labeled sketch of a logistic growth curve on unscaled axes: a horizontal axis labeled t and a vertical axis labeled f(t), both double-arrowed and carrying no numeric ticks. A dashed orange horizontal line stretches across the upper part of the plot, tagged y = c at its left end and joined by a black leader to the annotation Carrying capacity. The solid dark blue curve enters from the lower left, crosses the vertical axis at a marked point labeled (0, c/(1 + a)) and identified as the Initial value of population, steepens through the middle of the frame, then flattens and runs rightward just beneath the dashed line without meeting it. A filled dot on the steepest part of the rise is labeled with the coordinates (ln(a)/b, c/2) and connected by a leader to the words Point of maximum growth. The curve's formula, f(t) = c/(1 + ae^(-bx)), is printed in blue to the right of the upper bend. The three annotations single out what the reader is meant to take from the shape: where the curve starts, where its slope is greatest, and the ceiling it approaches. Together they establish that growth of this kind accelerates only until the population reaches half the carrying capacity, after which the rate of increase falls away as the curve saturates.

interactionPlan.concept: Logistic growth accelerates initially like exponential growth, reaches a maximum rate at half the carrying capacity, and then decelerates as it approaches its upper limit.

interactions.label: Time (t)
interactions.teaches: Moving along the curve reveals how the growth rate (indicated by the tangent slope) starts small, peaks exactly at c/2, and shrinks toward zero as the population approaches carrying capacity.

interactions.label: Growth rate (b)
interactions.teaches: Increasing the parameter 'b' makes the S-curve steeper and shifts the point of maximum growth earlier in time, controlling how rapidly the population transitions from exponential growth to saturation.

demo_steps.title: Initial growth
demo_steps.narration: At t=0, the population starts at its initial value. Early on, when the population is small and far from the carrying capacity, it grows at an increasing rate.

demo_steps.title: Maximum growth rate
demo_steps.narration: Drag time forward. The slope of the tangent line is steepest exactly at the inflection point (ln(a)/b, c/2). This is where the population is growing the fastest, precisely halfway to its maximum limit.

demo_steps.title: Approaching saturation
demo_steps.narration: Continue moving forward in time. As the distance to the carrying capacity shrinks, the growth rate (slope) slows down, causing the curve to level off.

demo_steps.title: Changing the growth parameter
demo_steps.narration: Now increase the growth rate b. The curve compresses horizontally, steepens, and the point of maximum growth shifts to an earlier time.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The defining characteristic of a logistic curve is that its growth rate is bounded by the available space—it accelerates until the population reaches exactly half the carrying capacity, and then inevitably decelerates.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Standard unscaled axes. The blue curve should clearly exhibit the S-shape, starting low on the left, inflecting smoothly, and asymptoting to the orange dashed line 'y = c'. Include all static text labels and leader lines exactly as shown (note: the image uses 'e^(-bx)' but standardizing to 'e^(-bt)' matches the horizontal axis). The dynamic elements (point, tangent line, vertical gap line) should be visually distinct (e.g., a dark red or grey for the tangent) and update smoothly as the sliders change. The inflection point coordinates are (ln(a)/b, c/2); for the demo, assume internal constants like c=10, a=10 so ln(10)/1 ~ 2.3.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for time t: the learner drags a marker along the logistic curve, the population value, tangent slope, and distance below y = c update together, making clear that growth is fastest at c/2 and slows as carrying capacity is approached.

authoredContext:
The graph in the figure shows how the growth rate changes over time. The graph increases from left to right, but the growth rate only increases until it reaches its point of maximum growth rate, at which point the rate of increase decreases.

Graph of f(t)=c/(1+ae^(-tx)). The carrying capacity is the asymptote at y=c. The initial value of population is (0, c/(1+a)). The point of maximum growth is (ln(a)/b, c/2).

discrepancies: The fraction bars in the math labels (e.g., the main equation and coordinates) are drawn manually with basic lines, resulting in uneven spacing and a noticeably short fraction bar for the main logistic equation.
Leader lines for the annotations ('Carrying capacity', 'Point of maximum growth', etc.) are straight arrows instead of the elegantly curved arrows used in the source.
The default view includes a red tangent line and a red dynamic point to support the interactive demo, which are absent in the static source image.
The source figure contains a typo in its equation exponent (-bx), which the generated figure correctly changes to match the function variable (-bt).
evaluation.notes: The figure successfully reproduces the logistic curve and provides an excellent pedagogical interaction showing the changing growth rate, though the manual canvas text rendering for fractions is slightly misaligned.
action_items: Lengthen the fraction bar line in the main equation so it spans the full width of the denominator '1 + a e^{-bt}'.
Replace the straight `drawLine` leader arrows with curved paths (using `quadraticCurveTo` or `bezierCurveTo`) to better match the source figure's annotations.

Hide the red tangent line and dynamic point on the initial load state so the default view acts as a perfect drop-in replacement for the static source image, revealing the dynamic elements only when the user interacts or advances the steps.
